# Promoted to repo memory: digest-signal

Cite these in .sofar/repo.md by qualified handle — `digest-signal M<n>` —
which is how `sofar doctor` sees that a promoted fact reached repo memory.

- **M1** (2026-08-30T05:47:54.584Z) — ADDING AN EVENT TYPE — the eight touch points, in order. Derived empirically from commit bacbb86 (session-driver 1.2, three driver events); every session that adds an event type currently rediscovers this by grepping a 1463-line fold.ts and a 683-line events.ts, which is minutes of archaeology per session.

1. docs/SPEC.md — contract FIRST; SPEC is authoritative over improvisation, so the envelope/payload shape lands here before code.
2. packages/schema/src/events.ts — payload interface plus the entry in the event union. This is the ONLY schema home (guard-rail); nothing outside packages/schema/src may define payloads.
3. packages/schema/test/schema.test.ts — validation coverage for the new payload.
4. packages/engine/src/core/fold.ts — a case in applyEvent's switch (31 cases as of 2026-08-30) plus any InitiativeState fields the event folds into. Note the ordering hazard already in the file: some derivations must run BEFORE applyEvent because they need the plan as it stands.
5. packages/engine/src/projections/templates/shared.ts — shared render helpers, if the event surfaces in more than one projection.
6. packages/engine/src/projections/templates/session.ts — session-file rendering.
7. packages/engine/src/projections/templates/status.ts — the SessionStart digest. Anything a future session must see at orientation goes here or it is invisible in practice.
8. packages/engine/test/<feature>-events.test.ts — a dedicated test file; the driver events shipped 219 lines of it.

Then `npm run build`, because of the trap already recorded above in this file: the in-session MCP tools run the GLOBAL install and will reject a payload type it does not know. To write events using the new type before publishing, bypass MCP and use the freshly built local engine — `node packages/engine/dist/cli.js event append <slug> --type … --payload …`.

Templates 5-7 are the ones most often missed, and missing them is silent: the event folds correctly and simply never appears in any projection, so the record looks complete while the next session cannot see the thing you recorded.
